GPT-2 XL is not the approved id openai-community/gpt2. The paper licences the code Apache-2.0 and "The Gen-A-tomic will be licensed under CC-BY". The tasksource card is apache-2.0; the released statements are the CC-BY Gen-A-tomic text.
I2D2.pass1_verdict: UNVERIFIED: generator — the opened card does not name the model that wrote the generics.

sms_spam.verdict: FAIL: rule 2 — UCI SMS Spam Collection: "A collection of 425 SMS spam messages was manually extracted from the Grumbletext Web site. This is a UK forum in which cell phone users make public claims about SMS spam messages". The same page says 3,375 NUS messages "were collected from volunteers who were made aware that their contributions were going to be made publicly available" and 450 come from Caroline Tagg's PhD thesis. Awareness is not a copyright grant, and the repository line "This dataset is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) license" does not licence those messages. The HF card licence is "unknown" and its licensing section has no grant.
sms_spam.pass1_verdict: UNVERIFIED: licence_spdx — cardData.license is "unknown" and "### Licensing Information" has no licence text. The SMS writers' grant was not found.

math_qa.pass1_verdict: UNVERIFIED: provenance — the opened card was not quoted past the licence tag apache-2.0, so the origin of the math word problems is not recorded here.

quartz.provenance: Crowdworkers wrote situated questions; the paired qualitative sentences were extracted by the authors from an unnamed corpus.
quartz.verdict: FAIL: rule 2 — Tafjord et al., arXiv:1909.03553: "expressing general qualitative relations were manually extracted by the authors from a large corpus using keyword search". The paper never names that corpus or a licence for it. Crowdworkers "author a situated" question, but the released paragraphs are the extracted sentences. The card says "The dataset is licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0)", which does not licence the corpus sentences. The paper's own line is only "License: arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive license".
quartz.pass1_verdict: UNVERIFIED: provenance — the opened README portion does not say where the question text comes from.

patent-phrase-similarity.provenance: Anchor phrases extracted from a patent corpus; some targets are other patent phrases and some are BERT mask predictions, then rated by people.
patent-phrase-similarity.verdict: FAIL: rule 2 — arXiv:2208.01171: "For each patent in the corpus we first extract important (salient) phrases." The paper does not name a licence for that corpus; "The full dataset is publicly available through Kaggle" is not a copyright grant. The paper line "License: CC BY 4.0" and the tasksource tag cc-by-4.0 do not licence the filers' phrases. Pre-generated targets also "use a BERT model (Devlin et al., 2019) to predict candidates for the masked portion", and that BERT checkpoint is not an approved generator (rule 3).
patent-phrase-similarity.pass1_verdict: UNVERIFIED: provenance — cardData.license is cc-by-4.0 and the card does not say where the patent phrases come from.

The paper's licence line is only "License: arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive license". balanced-copa.pass1_verdict: UNVERIFIED: provenance — Licensing Information is CC BY 4.0 and the opened text does not say who wrote the premises.

winodict.pass1_verdict: UNVERIFIED: provenance — the opened card does not describe the sentence source.

feasibilityQA.pass1_verdict: UNVERIFIED: provenance — cardData.license is mit and there is no sentence on the text.

The LexGLUE card YAML is cc-by-4.0 and its licensing section is "[More Information Needed]". The case.law terms pages are JavaScript shells with no licence sentence, so the opinions' copyright is not confirmed.
lex_glue/case_hold.pass1_verdict: UNVERIFIED: licence_spdx — YAML says cc-by-4.0 and "### Licensing Information" is "[More Information Needed]". The licence of the judicial opinions was not opened.

SDOH-NLI.provenance: Premises are sentences from MTSamples.com transcribed medical notes; hypotheses are author-rephrased social-determinant statements.
SDOH-NLI.verdict: UNVERIFIED: text_licence — Lelkes et al., arXiv:2310.18431: "we introduce a new, public SDOH dataset based on MTSamples.com, an online collection of transcribed medical reports" and "We then split each note section into sentences, resulting in 3,281 sentences ... 1,398 unique sentences." Hypotheses: "We rephrased each factor as a full English sentence". The paper and the GitHub LICENSE are CC-BY-4.0. mtsamples.com terms returned HTTP 500, so the notes' licence was not quoted. The authors' CC-BY-4.0 does not by itself licence those notes.
SDOH-NLI.pass1_verdict: UNVERIFIED: text_licence — LICENSE is Creative Commons Attribution 4.0, and the paper (arXiv 2310.18431) that would identify the clinical-note source was not opened.

The tasksource tag mit is not backed by a licence sentence.
corr2cause.pass1_verdict: UNVERIFIED: licence_spdx — the upstream card is "TODO" and the tasksource tag mit was not matched to a licence sentence. The sentence generator is also not named.

A GitHub search for a deepset-ai prompt-injections repository returned no repository, so neither the licence nor the writer of the strings is stated.
prompt-injections.pass1_verdict: UNVERIFIED: licence_spdx — the README body is only "[More Information needed]" while the API tag is apache-2.0, and the origin of the injection strings is not stated.
